# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 54 (Bi-Vb Pc54)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc54  
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 54  
**Title (English, from literature):** Eating more after refusing an offer  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 54 (Bi-Vb Pc54), titled *Pavārita* ("Eating more after refusing an offer"), stipulates that a Buddhist nun who consumes food after having finished her meal and refused further offerings commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [Hüsken 1997]. The origin narrative (*vorgeschichte*) of this rule is completely identical to the initial version of the corresponding rule for monks, Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 35 [Hüsken 1997]. While the origin story employs the phrasing *bhuttāvī pavāritā* ("having eaten and having refused"), the rule itself uses *nimantitā vā pavāritā vā* [Hüsken 1997]. The casuistry of both rules corresponds for the most part, though the non-offense clause (*anāpatti*) in the nun's rule shares only one specific exemption with the monk's rule—namely the permissible consumption of afternoon tonics or medicines (*yāmakālika*, *sattāhakālika*, *yāvajīvika*) when there is a requisite cause (*sati paccaye*) [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
